about: The shape of each road: a crisis at the start of chapter three, a low point before the finale, and a climax that opens the ending. Each one costs the captain something real (money, bonds, research, crew, guns) and leaves a flag the epilogue and Cargo 2 remember.

drama.trade.squeeze.title: The squeeze
text: The three corporations' trading houses have decided the independent haulers are a rounding error. This month they correct it: tech dumped below cost at every dock you use, until the small haulers sell their routes or their ships.
The Hansa convoy office panics and raises its dues by half, 'until the market settles'. Your loan officer calls to ask how you are. He has never asked before.

choices.say: Hold your lanes and eat the losses
Buy two Hansa bonds and stand with the convoy captains
Haul for the trading houses until it blows over

drama.trade.margin_call.title: Margin call
text: The bank at Alpha sells your ship's loan to a collector who works for the trading houses. He calls it in, all of it, by the end of the week. Until it is settled the convoy office will not give you a berth.
You are a week away from being a captain without a ship, and everybody at the bar knows it. The barman gives you the good glass. That is how you know it is bad.

The bank at Alpha sells your ship's loan to a collector who works for the trading houses. You know him: you hauled for him during the squeeze. He is very polite. He remembers your rates. He calls the loan in, all of it, by the end of the week.
Until it is settled the convoy office will not give you a berth. The barman gives you the good glass. That is how you know it is bad.

The bank at Alpha sells your ship's loan to a collector who works for the trading houses. He calls it in, all of it, by the end of the week. Until it is settled the convoy office will not give you a berth.
The convoy captains you stood with in the squeeze have heard. Nobody says anything yet. The barman gives you the good glass.

choices.say: Pay it all, today
Cash in your Hansa bonds
Ask the convoy captains to stand with you
Let the Grey Hats lose the paperwork

drama.trade.mint.title: The first Mark
text: The Hansa strikes its first Marks in a borrowed foundry at Gamma: pellets of iridium and osmium, each stamped with the weight of cargo it stands for.

The foundry foreman takes you aside. He can short every pellet by a hair. Nobody with ordinary scales would notice for ten years, and the Hansa needs the margin. He says this the way other people talk about the weather.

choices.say: Full weight, every pellet
Short them a hair; the Hansa needs it

drama.trade.run.title: A run on the Mark
text: Somebody has weighed a Mark and found it light. Or says so. By morning every convoy captain wants credits for their Marks, and the convoy office has credits for about a third of them.
A queue goes twice round the dock. Somebody has started selling soup to it.

Somebody has weighed a Mark and found it light. They are right, and you know exactly how light. By morning every convoy captain wants credits for their Marks, and the convoy office has credits for about a third of them.
A queue goes twice round the dock. The foundry foreman has taken a holiday.

choices.say: Weigh every Mark in public, on the dock
Buy Marks back with your own money
Let {broker.short} talk the queue down
Let it run its course

drama.trade.offer.title: A seat at the table
text: The trading houses ask you to dinner at Alpha: real tablecloth, real wine, and a contract. A seat on their board, and a share of every convoy, if the vote at Epsilon fails by one.
The wine is very good. That is the point of it.

choices.say: Refuse, and finish the wine
Take the seat (100,000 credits now)

drama.trade.vote.title: The vote
text: The convoy captains meet at Epsilon to vote the Mark into law. The trading houses send lawyers, the legions send observers, and somebody cuts the power to the hold. Forty captains vote by torchlight.
The count comes out one vote short, either way. Everybody looks at the captain with the most routes. Again.
The convoy captains meet at Epsilon to vote the Mark into law. The trading houses send lawyers, the legions send observers, and somebody cuts the power to the hold. Forty captains vote by torchlight.
You have a seat at the trading houses' table now, and everybody in the hold knows it. The count comes out one vote short. The missing vote is yours.
The convoy captains meet at Epsilon to vote the Mark into law. The trading houses send lawyers, the legions send observers, and somebody cuts the power to the hold. Forty captains vote by torchlight.
You never signed the charter. The count comes out one vote short, either way, and it turns out that makes you the only captain both sides will listen to.

choices.say: Speak for the Mark
Speak for the Mark anyway, and lose the seat
Buy the last vote (40,000 credits)
Walk out and let them count without you

drama.combat.left_behind.title: Left behind
text: Escort job: forty civilian haulers from Gamma to Alpha under a legion flag. At the jump point your two wingmen get a recall order, turn round and leave. Ten minutes later a pirate mothership comes out of the dark, exactly where the recall order said nobody would be.
Somebody sold this convoy. The haulers are calling you by name on an open channel. Most of them do not know your name; they are reading it off your hull.

choices.say: Hold the line
Lead them out through the debris
Follow the recall order

drama.combat.tribunal.title: The inquiry
text: The legions merge at a dinner you were not invited to. Your commission is 'under review', your ammunition is impounded pending an inquiry into the convoy at the jump point, and a tribunal wants your logs by Monday.
The inquiry has already decided who sold the convoy. It has decided it was you.

The legions merge at a dinner you were not invited to. Your commission is 'under review', your ammunition is impounded pending an inquiry into the convoy at the jump point, and a tribunal wants your logs by Monday.
The inquiry has already decided who sold the convoy: you. A strange thing to decide about the only ship that stayed.

The legions merge at a dinner you were not invited to. Your commission is 'under review', your ammunition is impounded pending an inquiry into the convoy at the jump point, and a tribunal wants your logs by Monday.
You did follow the recall. That is the trouble: so did whoever wrote it, and somebody has to have sold the convoy.

choices.say: Hand over your logs and tell it straight
Let {gunner.short} take the blame he offers to take
Take the ship and go dark

drama.combat.roll_call.title: Roll call
text: The merger ceremony is at Alpha: three logos, one new flag, every commander in dress uniform and every warship in parade order with its guns cold. That is when the pirate dreadnought arrives.
Your ammunition came back this morning; the inquiry lost your paperwork in your favour. Somebody on the open channel asks who is in charge. Nobody answers. Then everybody looks at your hull.

choices.say: Take the fight to them
Get the civilian ships out first

drama.discovery.fire.title: The fire
text: A fire in the sample store of the Stellar Institute at TRAPPIST-1. Nobody hurt. Every sample of the grey alloy is gone, with the notes, and the fire door was propped open with a chair from somebody else's lab.
{ancient_scholar.short} sits on the steps with a smoke-black notebook. 'Somebody does not want this to be true,' she says. 'Or wants it to be true only for them.'

choices.say: Pay for a new survey yourself
Take House Rostrom's offer of help
Find out whose chair it was (200 research points)

drama.discovery.not_proven.title: Not proven
text: The Academy's review board rules on the grey alloy: a natural formation, not shown to be made, further survey 'not a priority'. {ancient_scholar.short}'s grant is cancelled the same afternoon.
At customs your research logs are seized as unlicensed survey data. The officer is sorry. He has a form for being sorry.

The Academy's review board rules on the grey alloy: a natural formation, not shown to be made. {ancient_scholar.short}'s grant is cancelled the same afternoon, and House Rostrom's lawyers file your findings under the House's name. They send flowers.
At customs your research logs are seized as unlicensed survey data. The officer is sorry. He has a form for being sorry.

choices.say: Hand over the logs
Smuggle a copy out first
Publish everything, free, today

drama.discovery.burn.title: The long burn
text: {ancient_scholar.short} has the course: back along Scholz's Star's track to the edge of our own system, where the ring should be. Nobody will fund the flight, so nobody will be on it but you.
It is the longest burn your ship will ever make: out of the plane of the planets, no convoy, no depot. If the numbers are wrong you will find out a long way from anyone who could tow you.

choices.say: Burn on your own fuel (60 fuel)
Let {navigator.short} find a cheaper road (35 fuel)
Buy the fuel at any price (40,000 credits)
Fly it on House Rostrom's ship, under their name

after.held_the_lanes.text: The haulers who held their lanes through the squeeze still drink at a table nobody else uses. One of the chairs has your name on it. Somebody carved it.
after.held_the_lanes.title: After: held the lanes

after.cartel_hauler.text: The trading houses kept your rate card on file for forty years, as an example of a reasonable captain.
after.cartel_hauler.title: After: cartel hauler

after.captains_paid.text: The convoy captains who paid your margin call never asked for it back. Every year one of them sends a bill for a single credit, framed.
after.captains_paid.title: After: captains paid

after.won_the_vote.text: The record of the vote at Epsilon has forty names and one speech. Schoolchildren learn its first line. Nobody agrees on the second.
after.won_the_vote.title: After: won the vote

after.bought_the_vote.text: The captain whose vote you bought became the Hansa's first treasurer. He always said he had been cheap at the price.
after.bought_the_vote.title: After: bought the vote

after.walked_out.text: They counted without you and the Mark passed by one vote. Nobody ever learned which way you would have voted, which suited everybody.
after.walked_out.title: After: walked out

after.honest_mark.text: Every Mark from the first strike still weighs what it says. Collectors pay double for them, and weigh them first anyway.
after.honest_mark.title: After: honest mark

after.short_mark.text: The first Marks were a hair light. A Collective auditor found out ninety years later, wrote a polite report, and charged the Hansa for the scales.
after.short_mark.title: After: short mark

after.public_weighing.text: They weighed four thousand Marks on the dock at Epsilon, one by one, with a crowd counting along. It is a festival now. The soup is still sold.
after.public_weighing.title: After: public weighing

after.stood_behind_the_mark.text: You bought back Marks at face value until the queue ran out. The ones you kept are in a drawer on your ship. You never spent them.
after.stood_behind_the_mark.title: After: stood behind the mark

after.let_it_run.text: The run on the Mark lasted nine days and ruined two captains. The Mark survived it. People said that about the Mark, not about the captains.
after.let_it_run.title: After: let it run

after.fenn_talked.text: {broker.short} talked the queue down in one afternoon, mostly by telling it about his feet. Brokers still study the speech. Nobody has managed the feet.
after.fenn_talked.title: After: fenn talked

after.refused_the_seat.text: You refused the trading houses' seat and finished their wine. The bottle is on your shelf, empty, with the dinner date written on the label.
after.refused_the_seat.title: After: refused the seat

after.took_the_seat.text: You sat on the trading houses' board for eleven years and voted against them every time. They kept the seat warm for your successor, who did not.
after.took_the_seat.title: After: took the seat

after.turned_on_the_houses.text: The trading houses never forgave the vote at Epsilon. They named a ledger column after you: 'losses, unforeseeable'.
after.turned_on_the_houses.title: After: turned on the houses

after.held_the_line.text: The forty haulers from the jump point still send a crate every year, addressed only to your ship.
after.held_the_line.title: After: held the line

after.led_them_out.text: The lane you led forty haulers through is on the charts now, marked 'shortcut, not recommended'.
after.led_them_out.title: After: led them out

after.followed_the_recall.text: Whoever wrote the recall order rose high in the merged legion. Nobody asked you to testify, and you did not offer.
after.followed_the_recall.title: After: followed the recall

after.tadeo_took_blame.text: {gunner.short} served eight months in a legion brig for an order he never saw. He came out, found your ship, and asked whether the gunner's seat was still warm. It was.
after.tadeo_took_blame.title: After: tadeo took blame

after.led_the_defence.text: The dreadnought's bell hangs in the merged legion's mess. New pilots touch it for luck before their first patrol.
after.led_the_defence.title: After: led the defence

after.saved_the_civilians.text: Not one civilian ship was lost at Alpha. The legion's history gives the battle a chapter and the civilians a footnote; the civilians remember it the other way round.
after.saved_the_civilians.title: After: saved the civilians

after.found_the_chair.text: The chair that propped the fire door belonged to a security liaison from a firm that later became part of the Mandate. Nobody was charged. The chair sits in a cupboard you have the key to.
after.found_the_chair.title: After: found the chair

after.published_everything.text: Your logs, published free, were in every colony library within a year. The review board's ruling is in there too, as a footnote.
after.published_everything.title: After: published everything

after.rostrom_paper.text: The first paper on the ring carries House Rostrom's name in large letters and yours in the acknowledgements, between the caterer and the fuel supplier.
after.rostrom_paper.title: After: rostrom paper

after.paid_in_full.text: You paid the margin call in full and never borrowed again. The bank at Alpha still sends you a calendar every year, out of respect or fear.
after.paid_in_full.title: After: paid in full

after.sold_bonds.text: You sold your Hansa bonds to keep your ship. The captain who bought them sold them back to the Hansa ten years later for a farm.
after.sold_bonds.title: After: sold bonds

after.paperwork_lost.text: Your loan papers were never found. The Grey Hats sent an invoice for not finding them, which was also never found.
after.paperwork_lost.title: After: paperwork lost

after.told_the_truth.text: Your logs from the jump point are in the legion archive, unredacted. Nobody reads them; everybody knows they are there.
after.told_the_truth.title: After: told the truth

after.went_dark.text: For years the legion's wanted list carried your ship under a name that was nearly right. Nobody ever corrected it.
after.went_dark.title: After: went dark

after.funded_the_search.text: The survey you paid for after the fire found more alloy than the one that burned. The receipt is framed in the Institute's new store, next to the fire door, which closes now.
after.funded_the_search.title: After: funded the search

after.logs_seized.text: Your seized logs turned up forty years later in a customs auction, sold as 'ship's diary, dull'.
after.logs_seized.title: After: logs seized

after.kept_a_copy.text: The copy you smuggled past customs is the one every later survey quotes. The original is still in a customs vault, with a form attached.
after.kept_a_copy.title: After: kept a copy

after.flew_it_ourselves.text: You flew the long burn on your own fuel. The ship never quite lost the frost on its forward plates, and you never had it cleaned.
after.flew_it_ourselves.title: After: flew it ourselves

after.bought_the_burn.text: The fuel for the long burn cost more than the ship. The depot named a tank after you, as a joke at first.
after.bought_the_burn.title: After: bought the burn

after.sisters_road.text: {navigator.short}'s road to the edge of the system is still flown. Everybody calls it the Sister's Road except the Solarians, who call it obvious.
after.sisters_road.title: After: sisters road

after.held_the_line_lost.title: After: held the line, lost
after.held_the_line_lost.text: You lost the fight at the jump point and the mothership took a third of the convoy. The other two thirds got home because you were in its way. Their captains still argue about whether that counts. They buy you drinks while they argue.

after.led_the_defence_lost.title: After: led the defence, lost
after.led_the_defence_lost.text: The dreadnought beat you at Alpha and left with its holds full, but it left. The new legion flew its first flag full of the holes it made that day, and never replaced it.
